pluss::timeline::epoch¶

Back to Timeline Factory API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline pluss::timeline::epoch(integer_range sizes = {})

Allocate A Known Shape At Tick Zero¶

epoch() allocates an owning Timeline whose every lane is the Unix epoch: the valid instant represented by epoch nanosecond 0, displayed in UTC as 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000000000+00:00.

This factory is useful when shape must be established before meaningful instants are assigned or transformed. Epoch is ordinary data, not an absent instant and not an uninitialized placeholder. Code that must represent absence should construct Timeline::kNaT explicitly with from_epoch() or full().

Omitting sizes creates a rank-zero scalar. {n} creates a vector, and two or three extents create a matrix or rank-three value. Zero-length axes are retained as geometry. The public Timeline contract supports ranks zero through three.

The returned value owns fresh contiguous int64 storage. Construction is linear in the number of elements and initializes the storage without parsing text or converting through floating point.

Example 1: The Default Is A Scalar¶

const auto origin = pluss::timeline::epoch();
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(origin, "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"1970-01-01T00:00:00.000000000+00:00"

An empty shape list means rank zero and one lane; it does not mean zero lanes.

Example 2: A Vector Of Exact Zero Ticks¶

const auto values = pluss::timeline::epoch({4});
std::cout << pluss::series::print(values.epoch_nanos()) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 0, 0, 0]

Example 3: Rank-Three Geometry¶

const auto block = pluss::timeline::epoch({1, 2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::series::print(block.epoch_nanos()) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[1,2,2], strides=[4,2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data[0, :, :] =
⎡ 0 0 ⎤
⎣ 0 0 ⎦

Example 4: Zero-Length Axes Preserve Shape¶

const auto empty_rows = pluss::timeline::epoch({2, 0});
std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(empty_rows) << '\n';

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[2, 0], tz=UTC)[  ]
[  ]

The value is defined and has shape [2, 0], rank two, and zero elements. This is useful in generic shape-preserving code because the nonempty axis is not discarded.

Validation And Failure¶

Every extent must be nonnegative, rank must not exceed three, and the product of the extents must fit in signed 64-bit shape arithmetic. Validation happens before allocation.

try {
  (void)pluss::timeline::epoch({1, 1, 1, 1});
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "rejected\n";
}

Output¶

rejected

See Also¶

  • full: allocate a shape filled with any scalar instant.

  • full_like: obtain shape from an existing Timeline.

  • from_epoch: construct from supplied epoch nanoseconds.
